[project]
name = "vllm-hust-knorm"
description = "KNorm key-L2-norm KV-cache compression for vLLM-HUST, as a runtime-loadable extension bundle"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [{ name = "vLLM-HUST KNorm maintainers" }]
dependencies = []
dynamic = ["version"]

# Runtime plugin hook. vLLM calls it in every process during plugin
# loading; registration installs the patches, VLLM_KNORM_ENABLED=1 is
# the explicit activation switch.
[project.entry-points."vllm.general_plugins"]
"vllm-hust-knorm" = "vllm_hust_knorm.bootstrap:register_plugins"

# Extension Manager discovery (static manifest locator; the manager
# reads the JSON next to this package without importing any
# implementation). Registration name must equal the extension_id.
[project.entry-points."vllm_hust.extension_bundles"]
"org.vllm-hust.knorm" = "vllm_hust_knorm.manifests"

"""``vllm.general_plugins`` dynamic-load entry point.

After installation, vLLM imports this entry point in every process
(process 0, engine core and workers) during plugin loading, and calls
``register_plugins()``. Registration installs the runtime patches but
does not enable compression: only ``VLLM_KNORM_ENABLED=1`` (plus
prefix caching disabled) activates Knorm.

Failure mode: when this process is not a vllm host the hook is a no-op;
when the host conflicts with an in-tree ``vllm.knorm`` or lacks the
required surfaces, activation raises and vLLM logs the exception —
fail closed, never a silent half-install.

def register_plugins() -> list[str]:
    """Register Knorm in vLLM hosts; no-op elsewhere."""
    if detect_host() is None:
        return []

    from .core.activation import activate

    info = activate()
    print(
        "[vllm-hust-knorm] runtime patches registered; activate with "
        "VLLM_KNORM_ENABLED=1 and --no-enable-prefix-caching "
        f"(status={info.get('status')})",
        flush=True,
    )

# Host surfaces the runtime patches bind to. Kept in one place so the
# contract tests and HOST_CONTRACT.md stay in sync with the adapter.
# An "attr1|attr2" entry means any one of the alternatives satisfies
# the contract (host generations renamed the free-block queue class).
REQUIRED_SURFACES = (
    "vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager:register_all_kvcache_specs",
    "vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager:FullAttentionManager",
    "vllm.v1.kv_cache_spec_registry:KVCacheSpecRegistry",
    "vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils:FreeKVCacheBlockQueue|FreeQueue",
    "vllm.v1.core.block_pool:BlockPool",
    "vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler:Scheduler",
    "vllm.v1.worker.gpu_model_runner:GPUModelRunner",
)

def require_no_in_tree_knorm() -> None:
    """Fail closed when the host already ships an in-tree ``vllm.knorm``.

    vLLM-HUST builds of the 0.23 seam era embed the legacy in-tree Knorm
    module behind try-imports. Installing this plugin next to them would
    double-provide the feature; the guide forbids silently ignoring the
    conflict, so activation refuses with instructions. A stale directory
    without ``__init__.py`` (namespace-only) is not a conflict.
    """
    if real_module_present("vllm.knorm"):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "vllm-hust-knorm refuses to activate: this vLLM install "
            "already ships an in-tree 'vllm.knorm' module. Remove the "
            "in-tree module (use a knorm-free vLLM-HUST build) or "
            "uninstall one of the two implementations; running both is "
            "unsupported."
        )


def require_host_surfaces() -> None:
    """Fail closed when any host surface required by the patches is
    missing, naming every missing symbol."""
    missing: list[str] = []
    for surface in REQUIRED_SURFACES:
        module_name, _, attr = surface.partition(":")
        try:
            spec = importlib.util.find_spec(module_name)
        except (ImportError, ValueError):
            spec = None
        if spec is None:
            missing.append(surface)
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "vllm-hust-knorm requires host surfaces that are not "
            "importable in this process: "
            + ", ".join(missing)
            + ". See HOST_CONTRACT.md for the verified host baselines; "
            "compatibility must not be assumed for other builds."

def should_activate(enable_prefix_caching: bool) -> bool:
    """Single source of truth for Knorm activation.

    Migrated verbatim in rule from the in-tree fix for legacy issue #163
    (PR #214): manager registration and the runner-side attention wrapper
    must consult the same predicate, otherwise a half-enabled state adds
    per-forward norm overhead with no consumer. Knorm is active only when
    ALL of:

    - ``VLLM_KNORM_ENABLED`` is true;
    - ``compression_ratio < 1.0`` (matches :attr:`KnormConfig.is_active`);
    - prefix caching is disabled (mutually exclusive; PR #134).
    """
    return env_enabled() and env_compression_ratio() < 1.0 and not enable_prefix_caching

[project]
name = "vllm-hust-qos-scheduler"
version = "0.1.0.dev0"
description = "vllm-hust-qos-scheduler inert vLLM-HUST contract descriptor"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=8", "ruff>=0.12", "vllm-hust-ext==0.2.0.dev0"]

[project.entry-points."vllm_hust.extension_bundles"]
"org.vllm-hust.qos-scheduler" = "vllm_hust_qos_scheduler"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/vllm_hust_qos_scheduler"]

# QoS scheduler host contract proposal

The extracted request model and ordering policy are independent of vLLM API and
scheduler classes. Runtime activation requires:

1. `vllm.request.qos-metadata.v1`: parse bounded TTFT/TBT/TTLT SLO fields at the
   API boundary and attach immutable metadata to the engine request.
2. `vllm.scheduler.request-snapshot.v1`: expose token counters, priority, arrival
   time, and local monotonic QoS state without exposing a mutable Request object.
3. `vllm.scheduler.ordering-policy.v1`: register waiting/running ordering keys;
   the extension may reorder but must not create a separate token budget.
4. `vllm.scheduler.output-observer.v1`: report generated-token and completion
   timestamps for SLO accounting.

Phase-one activation must fail closed for pipeline/data/context/expert parallel,
speculative decoding, KV disaggregation, LoRA, and other combinations not covered
by hardware and correctness tests. The API remains backward-compatible because
requests without QoS metadata retain native scheduling.

[project]
name = "vllm-ascend-split-batch"
version = "0.1.0.dev0"
description = "vllm-ascend-split-batch inert vLLM-HUST contract descriptor"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=8", "ruff>=0.12", "vllm-hust-ext==0.2.0.dev0"]

[project.entry-points."vllm_hust.extension_bundles"]
"org.vllm-hust.split-batch-full-graph" = "vllm_ascend_split_batch"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/vllm_ascend_split_batch"]

# Split-batch host contract proposal

The extracted planner is pure and default-off. Runtime activation requires:

1. `vllm.graph.runtime-key.v1`: validated, bounded opaque graph metadata;
2. `vllm.forward.split-context.v1`: per-forward split mode and stream identity;
3. `vllm.ascend.graph-pool.v1`: separately owned main/parallel graph pools;
4. `vllm.worker.split-executor.v1`: execute a committed plan and restore all
   buffers/context on success, error, or cancellation.

The provider must reject speculative decoding, LoRA, MLA, M-RoPE, non-uniform
decode, unsupported graph modes, and unknown capture sizes. It must never lazily
capture an unbounded key set or modify global forward context outside a scoped
context manager.

[project]
name = "vllm-hust-unified-comm"
version = "0.1.0.dev0"
description = "vllm-hust-unified-comm inert vLLM-HUST contract descriptor"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=8", "ruff>=0.12", "vllm-hust-ext==0.2.0.dev0"]

[project.entry-points."vllm_hust.extension_bundles"]
"org.vllm-hust.unified-communication" = "vllm_hust_unified_comm"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/vllm_hust_unified_comm"]

# Unified communication host contract proposal

The extracted registry and decision policies are independent of torch, NCCL,
HCCL, and vLLM. Runtime activation requires a vLLM provider implementing:

1. `vllm.communication.backend.v1`: register a backend factory by unique name and
   device type; registration must reject collisions.
2. `vllm.communication.group.v1`: provide immutable ranks, local rank, world size,
   device identity, and existing process-group handles.
3. `vllm.communication.collectives.v1`: delegate individual collectives with an
   explicit failure result so the host can use its native fallback.
4. `vllm.communication.topology.v1`: provide topology facts used for decisions;
   the extension must not probe or reconfigure NICs and drivers itself.

GroupCoordinator remains lifecycle owner. The extension must not create a second
default process group, destroy host-owned communicators, or silently replace an
existing backend. Direct NCCL/HCCL C-API implementations require separate native
packages and hardware-specific validation.

findings.fact: Package dependencies are empty, but activation requires seven vLLM module/class surfaces and guards against an in-tree duplicate.
findings.ecpa_existing: Explicit host/protocol requirements and version checks can represent known prerequisites.
findings.ecpa_gap: No automatic private-symbol dependency discovery; declared version ranges do not prove symbols or ABI. Guard currently checks module specs, not every named attribute.
findings.experiment: Compare package resolution with exact-module/symbol preflight, then actual activation. Missing/renamed symbols stay an independently observed negative; do not infer runtime support from version.

findings.fact: Registration installs patches, while compression requires env enabled, ratio<1, and prefix caching off. Runner freezes that predicate during initialization.
findings.ecpa_existing: Separate discovered/loaded/invoked/effective states and bind effects to execution obligations.
findings.ecpa_gap: The current vocabulary alone does not prove compression, representation correctness, or equivalence across configurations.
findings.experiment: Freeze enabled/disabled and prefix-cache configurations before each independent start; measure real cache effect above the compression threshold, not only HTTP200.

findings.fact: KNorm wraps Scheduler.update_from_output and explicitly rebinds already-imported registration aliases from sys.modules.
findings.ecpa_existing: Canonical resource ownership and explicit ordering can reject declared double ownership.
findings.ecpa_gap: The planner does not infer hidden wrappers or prove wrapper commutativity; overlapping symbols alone do not prove incompatibility.
findings.experiment: Cross both MOD registration orders and early/late host import. Trace original-call chain, per-MOD invocation, and shared KV state; use singleton controls.

findings.fact: The frozen package describes itself as inert, exposes an import_only policy, has no activation entry points, and proposes four host protocols.
findings.ecpa_existing: An inspect-only outcome can avoid promoting a descriptor to runtime effectiveness.
findings.ecpa_gap: A manifest cannot supply the missing API-boundary metadata and scheduler binding.
findings.experiment: Report discoverability separately from host-executable eligibility. QoS+BidKV is a candidate until both effects and the common scheduler authority are bound.
findings.ground_truth: source-observed-inert-descriptor; not a native compatible pair

findings.fact: The pure split planner requires scoped forward context, separate graph pools and a worker executor; its contract excludes speculative decoding and other unsupported graph modes.
findings.ecpa_existing: Host capabilities and resource ownership can encode known requirements and exclusions.
findings.ecpa_gap: No demonstrated native provider for this frozen descriptor; no automatic proof of buffer restoration or graph safety.
findings.experiment: Keep split+speculative as a source-restriction candidate; demand a real executor before any positive composition or graph-performance cell.
findings.ground_truth: source-observed-restriction, not an injected native failure

findings.fact: Unified communication exports an import_only registry/strategy. Its proposed provider must preserve GroupCoordinator ownership and must not create a second default process group.
findings.ecpa_existing: Capability, lifecycle authority and resource owner declarations express the intended boundary.
findings.ecpa_gap: A Python registry cannot attest HCCL collective behavior or communicator lifetime.
findings.experiment: Classify missing provider/native backend as unsupported or unknown; do not turn a successful pure-policy import into composition success.
